intro: This lesson is about small words with a big job: a/an, the, and this, that, these, those. Indonesian often doesn't need them ('Saya punya mobil'), but English does ('I have a car'). Warm-up: look around you and name one thing with a or an, like 'a phone' or 'an umbrella'.
teachingNotes: Biggest Indonesian interference: no articles, so learners drop a/an (*'I have car', *'My brother is teacher'). One countable thing always needs a/an, my, this, that or the. Plurals need no a/an (two cars).

a or an depends on the first SOUND, not the letter: an egg, an orange, an hour; a university, a uniform. With an adjective, look at the adjective: an old car, a big apple. Common error: *'She is a engineer'.

the = the listener knows which one: it was mentioned before (I have a cat. The cat is white.), there is only one (the sun, the moon, the sky), or it's clear in the place (Please close the door. Where is the toilet?). Indonesian -nya or 'itu' often does this job (pintunya = the door).

this/these = near (ini), that/those = far (itu). this/that + one thing, these/those + two or more. Common error: *'This books are mine' → These books. English puts the word BEFORE the noun (this book), Indonesian after it (buku ini). Don't use a/an with them: *'this a book'.

Limits: only to be, have and simple sentences from earlier lessons. Do not teach zero article with uncountable/general plurals in depth, 'the' with names of places, or 'one/ones'. No past or future forms.
Indonesian classifiers (sebuah, seorang, sebutir, seekor) all become a/an; tell learners there's one word for all of them.
Indonesian doesn't have to mark plural (buku ini = one book or many books); English must choose this book / these books. This is the root of *'this books'.
'This is a book' (a sentence: Ini sebuah buku) vs 'this book' (a phrase: buku ini) explains why 'this a book' is wrong.

Describing words go before the noun in English (the red shirt = kemeja yang merah); point it out when it appears, don't drill it (adjectives come next lesson). 'Where is the toilet?' is fine everywhere; Americans often say restroom or bathroom.

keyPoints.title: the: you both know which one
keyPoints.explanation: Use the when the thing was mentioned before, when there is only one (the sun, the moon), or when it's clear which one in the place (the door, the toilet). First time: a/an. Second time: the.

examples.en: Budi has a car. The car is red.
Excuse me, where is the toilet?

keyPoints.title: this, that, these, those
keyPoints.explanation: this (one, near) and these (two or more, near) = ini. that (one, far) and those (two or more, far) = itu. They go BEFORE the noun: this book = buku ini.

examples.en: These shirts are cheap, and those shirts are expensive.
examples.id: Kemeja-kemeja ini murah, dan kemeja-kemeja itu mahal.

keyPoints.title: Don't forget a/an
keyPoints.explanation: One countable thing needs a or an (or my, this, the …). Indonesian sebuah, seorang and sebutir are all just a/an. Use an before a vowel SOUND (an egg, an hour) and a before a consonant sound (a car, a university).

examples.en: We have an hour for lunch.
examples.id: Kita punya waktu satu jam untuk makan siang.

guidedPractice.hint: Nurse starts with an 'n' sound, a consonant sound.

assessment.prompt: Correct the sentence: My brother is teacher.
assessment.rubric: Correct: My brother is a teacher. 'an teacher' = 50. No article = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with a or an: Sari has ___ umbrella.
assessment.rubric: Correct: an (umbrella starts with a vowel sound). 'a' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with a, an or the: Pak Hasan has a shop in Bogor. ___ shop is small.
assessment.rubric: Correct: The (the shop was mentioned before). 'A' = 0.

assessment.prompt: Complete with a, an or the: It's very hot. ___ sun is strong today.
assessment.rubric: Correct: The (there is only one sun). 'A' = 0.

acceptableAnswers: is that the bus to bandung

assessment.prompt: You are holding the shoes in your hands. Correct the sentence: This shoes are new.
assessment.rubric: Correct: These shoes are new (plural and near). 'Those shoes' = 50 (plural but far). Keeping 'This' = 0.

blocks.text: In Indonesian you can say *Saya punya mobil*. In English, **one** countable thing (a thing you can count: *one car, two cars*) needs a small word in front: **a**, **an**, **my**, **this**, **the** … So: **I have a car.** Not 'I have car'. **a/an** means 'one': Indonesian *sebuah*, *seorang*, *sebutir* are all just **a/an** in English. With two or more, add **-s** and no a/an: *two cars*.

id.text: Dalam bahasa Indonesia kamu bisa bilang *Saya punya mobil*. Dalam bahasa Inggris, **satu** benda yang bisa dihitung (benda yang bisa kamu hitung: *one car, two cars*) butuh kata kecil di depannya: **a**, **an**, **my**, **this**, **the** … Jadi: **I have a car.** Bukan 'I have car'. **a/an** artinya 'satu': *sebuah*, *seorang*, *sebutir* dalam bahasa Inggris semuanya cukup **a/an**. Kalau dua atau lebih, tambahkan **-s** tanpa a/an: *two cars*.

rows.id: Itu rumah tua. (old dibaca 'OULD', diawali bunyi vokal → an)
rows.note: look at the next word: old

blocks.text: **a** or **an** depends on the first **sound**, not the letter. **an** before a vowel sound: *an egg, an orange, an hour* (h is silent). **a** before a consonant sound: *a book, a university* (university starts with a 'yu' sound, like *you*). So it's **an engineer**, not 'a engineer'. a/an listens to the word **right after it**, even when that's a describing word: *a house*, but *an old house*.

id.text: **a** atau **an** bergantung pada **bunyi** pertama, bukan hurufnya. **an** sebelum bunyi vokal: *an egg, an orange, an hour* (h tidak dibaca). **a** sebelum bunyi konsonan: *a book, a university* (university dibaca 'yu-ni-ver-si-ti', diawali bunyi 'y' seperti *you*). Jadi **an engineer**, bukan 'a engineer'. a/an melihat kata **tepat sesudahnya**, walaupun itu kata yang menjelaskan: *a house*, tapi *an old house*.

blocks.explain: The h in hour is silent, so the first sound is a vowel: an hour.

id.explain: Huruf h pada hour tidak dibaca, jadi bunyi pertamanya vokal: an hour.

blocks.text:
In Indonesian, a letter almost always has the same sound: **u** is always read 'u'. In English it **isn't**: one letter can have different sounds. That's why a/an **doesn't look at the first letter you write**. It listens to the **first sound you say**.

So don't look, **say it**: read the word out loud and listen to how it starts.
- It starts with a **vowel sound** (your mouth is open: a, e, i, o, u) → **an**.
- It starts with a **consonant sound** (b, k, m, **y**, **w** …) → **a**.

id.text:
Di bahasa Indonesia, satu huruf hampir selalu punya satu bunyi: huruf **u** selalu dibaca 'u'. Di bahasa Inggris **tidak begitu**: satu huruf bisa punya bunyi yang berbeda-beda. Karena itu, aturan a/an **tidak melihat huruf pertama yang ditulis**, tapi **mendengar bunyi pertama yang diucapkan**.

Jadi jangan dilihat, tapi **ucapkan**: baca katanya dengan suara keras, lalu dengarkan bunyi awalnya.
- Diawali **bunyi vokal** (mulut langsung terbuka: a, e, i, o, u) → pakai **an**.
- Diawali **bunyi konsonan** (b, k, m, **y**, **w** …) → pakai **a**.

rows.id: dibaca 'AW-er', h tidak dibaca → bunyi 'a' (vokal) → an
dibaca 'ON-est', h tidak dibaca → bunyi 'o' (vokal) → an

blocks.text: Two tricks to remember. **u** at the start is often said 'you', and 'you' starts with a **y** sound, a consonant: *a university, a uniform, a useful app*. And sometimes **h** is not said at all, so the word really starts with a vowel sound: *an hour, an honest man*. In most words h is said (*a house, a hotel, a hospital*). When you're not sure, say the word out loud: trust your ears, not your eyes.

id.text: Dua trik supaya gampang ingat. Huruf **u** di awal kata sering dibaca 'yu', dan 'yu' diawali bunyi **y**, yaitu konsonan: *a university, a uniform, a useful app*. Lalu kadang huruf **h** tidak dibaca sama sekali, jadi katanya sebenarnya diawali bunyi vokal: *an hour, an honest man*. Di kebanyakan kata, h tetap dibaca (*a house, a hotel, a hospital*). Kalau ragu, ucapkan katanya dengan keras: percayai telingamu, bukan matamu.

blocks.prompt: Pak Budi wears ___ uniform to work.
blocks.explain: Uniform is said 'YU-ni-form'. It starts with a 'y' sound, a consonant sound, so it's a uniform, even though the first letter is u.

id.explain: Uniform dibaca 'YU-ni-form'. Bunyi pertamanya 'y', yaitu bunyi konsonan, jadi a uniform, walaupun huruf pertamanya u.

blocks.text: Use **the** when the listener knows **which one**: 1) you said it before (*I have a cat. **The** cat is white.*), 2) there is **only one** (*the sun, the moon, the sky*), 3) it's clear in the place (*Please open **the** door. Where is **the** toilet?*). In Indonesian, **-nya** or **itu** often does the same job: *pintunya* = **the door**.

id.text: Pakai **the** kalau pendengar tahu **yang mana**: 1) sudah kamu sebut sebelumnya (*I have a cat. **The** cat is white.*), 2) hanya ada **satu** (*the sun, the moon, the sky*), 3) jelas di tempat itu (*Please open **the** door. Where is **the** toilet?*). Dalam bahasa Indonesia, **-nya** atau **itu** sering punya fungsi yang sama: *pintunya* = **the door**.

rows.en: Budi has a car. The car is red.
The teacher is in the office.

blocks.text: First time: **a/an**. After that: **the**. *We have a new teacher. **The** teacher is from Medan.*

id.text: Pertama kali disebut: **a/an**. Setelah itu: **the**. *We have a new teacher. **The** teacher is from Medan.*

blocks.prompt: Look at ___ sky! It's very blue.
blocks.explain: There is only one sky, so we say the sky.

id.explain: Langit hanya ada satu, jadi kita bilang the sky.

blocks.text:
Point at things with four words. **Near** you: **this** (one) and **these** (two or more) = *ini*. **Far** from you: **that** (one) and **those** (two or more) = *itu*. In English the word comes **before** the noun (the name of the thing: *book, house*): *buku ini* = **this book**, *rumah itu* = **that house**.

Indonesian doesn't have to show 'many': *buku ini* can be one book or ten books. English **must** choose: one → **this book**, many → **these books** (with -s on the noun too).

id.text:
Tunjuk benda dengan empat kata. **Dekat** denganmu: **this** (satu) dan **these** (dua atau lebih) = *ini*. **Jauh** darimu: **that** (satu) dan **those** (dua atau lebih) = *itu*. Dalam bahasa Inggris katanya ada **sebelum** kata benda (nama bendanya: *book, house*): *buku ini* = **this book**, *rumah itu* = **that house**.

Bahasa Indonesia tidak harus menunjukkan 'banyak': *buku ini* bisa satu buku atau sepuluh buku. Bahasa Inggris **harus** memilih: satu → **this book**, banyak → **these books** (kata bendanya juga pakai -s).

blocks.text: Plural noun (two or more) → plural word: **these books**, **those books**. 'This books' is wrong. And no a/an after them. **This is a book** is a full sentence (*Ini sebuah buku*: is joins the two parts). **this book** is just a name for one thing (*buku ini*). 'this a book' mixes the two, so it's wrong.

id.text: Kata benda jamak (dua atau lebih) → kata penunjuk jamak: **these books**, **those books**. 'This books' salah. Dan jangan pakai a/an setelahnya. **This is a book** adalah kalimat lengkap (*Ini sebuah buku*: is menyambungkan dua bagiannya). **this book** hanya sebutan untuk satu benda (*buku ini*). 'this a book' mencampur keduanya, jadi salah.

blocks.prompt: You show your friend some photos on your phone. ___ are my kids.
blocks.explain: The photos are near you (in your hand) and there are two or more: these.

id.explain: Fotonya dekat denganmu (di tanganmu) dan jumlahnya lebih dari satu: these.

blocks.text: At a market or a shop you use all these words together: you point (**this, those**), you ask about one thing (**a/an**), and you talk about something you both can see (**the**). Notice that the describing word comes **before** the thing: *kemeja merah* = **the red shirt**.

id.text: Di pasar atau toko kamu memakai semua kata ini bersama-sama: kamu menunjuk (**this, those**), bertanya tentang satu benda (**a/an**), dan membicarakan benda yang sama-sama kalian lihat (**the**). Perhatikan, kata yang menjelaskan ada **sebelum** bendanya: *kemeja merah* = **the red shirt**.

rows.en: How much is this shirt? — It's Rp75.000.

rows.note: the one we can both see; red before shirt

blocks.prompt: You are in a restaurant. Excuse me, where is ___ toilet?
blocks.explain: The restaurant has its own toilet and you both know which one, so say the toilet. (Americans often say restroom or bathroom.)

id.explain: Restorannya punya toilet sendiri dan kalian sama-sama tahu yang mana, jadi bilang the toilet. (Orang Amerika sering bilang restroom atau bathroom.)

suggestedQuestions: Why is it 'an hour' but 'a university'?
When do I use a and when the?
Is 'ini' always this, and 'itu' always that?

id.intro: Pelajaran ini tentang kata-kata kecil dengan tugas besar: a/an, the, serta this, that, these, those. Bahasa Indonesia sering tidak membutuhkannya ('Saya punya mobil'), tapi bahasa Inggris membutuhkannya ('I have a car'). Pemanasan: lihat sekelilingmu dan sebutkan satu benda dengan a atau an, misalnya 'a phone' atau 'an umbrella'.
suggestedQuestions: Kapan pakai a dan kapan pakai the?
Apakah 'ini' selalu this, dan 'itu' selalu that?

assessment.art-1: Perbaiki kalimatnya: My brother is teacher.
assessment.art-2: Lengkapi dengan a atau an: Sari has ___ umbrella.
assessment.art-3: Lengkapi dengan a, an atau the: Pak Hasan has a shop in Bogor. ___ shop is small.
assessment.art-4: Lengkapi dengan a, an atau the: It's very hot. ___ sun is strong today.
assessment.art-5: Kamu menunjuk sebuah bus yang jauh, di seberang jalan. Lengkapi dengan this, that, these atau those: Is ___ the bus to Bandung?
assessment.art-6: Kamu sedang memegang sepatunya. Perbaiki kalimatnya: This shoes are new.
